events.title: The Intertestamental Period Begins
events.description: 400 years without prophetic word. The Jews are ruled by Persians, Greeks, and Romans.

events.title: Alexander the Great's Conquests
events.description: Alexander the Great conquers Persia and the entire Middle East, including Israel. Greek culture spreads.

events.title: Alexander Visits Jerusalem
events.description: Alexander the Great visits Jerusalem. According to Josephus, the high priest shows him Daniel's prophecies.

events.title: The Death of Alexander
events.description: Alexander dies in Babylon at only 32 years old. The empire is divided among his generals.

events.title: Ptolemaic Rule over Israel
events.description: Israel comes under Ptolemaic (Egyptian) rule. The Jews enjoy relative peace and religious freedom.

events.title: The Septuagint is translated
events.description: The Old Testament is translated into Greek in Alexandria - the Septuagint (LXX).

events.title: Seleucid rule over Israel
events.description: Israel comes under Seleucid (Syrian) control after the Battle of Panias.

events.title: Antiochus IV persecutes the Jews
events.description: Antiochus IV Epiphanes forbids Jewish religious practice and desecrates the temple.

events.title: The Abomination of Desolation
events.description: Antiochus sets up an altar to Zeus in the temple and sacrifices a pig - the abomination of desolation.

events.title: The Maccabean Revolt
events.description: Mattathias and his sons begin the revolt against the Seleucids. Judas Maccabeus leads the fight.

events.title: The Temple Rededicated - Hanukkah
events.description: Judas Maccabeus cleanses and rededicates the temple. This is commemorated in the festival of Hanukkah.

events.title: The Hasmonean Dynasty
events.description: The Maccabean family establishes the Hasmonean dynasty, which rules an independent Israel.

events.title: The Pharisees and Sadducees
events.description: The religious groups of the Pharisees and Sadducees emerge with different theological positions.

events.title: The Essenes and Qumran
events.description: The Essene community establishes itself at Qumran and writes the Dead Sea Scrolls.

events.title: Pompey Conquers Jerusalem
events.description: The Roman general Pompey conquers Jerusalem. Israel becomes part of the Roman Empire.

events.title: Herod Becomes King
events.description: Rome appoints Herod the Great as king of Judea. He is Idumean and not fully Jewish.

events.title: Herod Expands the Temple
events.description: Herod begins a massive expansion and beautification of the temple in Jerusalem.

events.title: Pax Romana - The Roman Peace
events.description: Augustus's era of peace creates stable conditions that later facilitate the spread of the gospel.

events.title: Roman Roads and Infrastructure
events.description: The Roman road network prepares the world for the rapid spread of the gospel.

events.title: Greek as a Common Language
events.description: Greek (Koine) has become the common language throughout the Mediterranean region.

events.title: The Expectation of the Messiah
events.description: A strong expectation of the coming of the Messiah grows among the Jews under foreign rule.
